newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rights groups urge Europe to put on pressure.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rights groups urge Europe to put on pressure.

text.p: On the eve of the start of talks on a trade treaty, a coalition of Mexican human rights groups urged the European Union to step up pressure on Mexico to stop torture and other rights abuses.

"We want to bring to your attention our most profound concern over the deterioration of the human rights situation in Mexico," a letter sent to Brussels by the National Network of Civil Organisations said.
"We urge the European Union, during its talks with Mexico, to pressure its government to introduce measures to remedy the increase in the violation of these rights."
Mexico and the European Union were due to start talks on Tuesday on a trans-Atlantic trade treaty, after Mexico bowed to EU pressure to include a human rights clause in a deal.

The Network, which is spearheaded by the non-governmental Miguel Agustin Pro Juarez AC Human Rights Centre, said institutional impunity was widespread in Mexico, and it attacked the growing use of the army in civilian police work.

"Disappearances, extra-judicial executions and arbitrary detentions have become more frequent day by day, and torture is a standard technique in police interrogations," the letter, sent to European Commission Representative Manuel Marin Gonzalez and members of the European Parliament, said.
The Mexican government has denied a build-up in human rights abuses, and has been anxious to keep the issue on the back-burner in the talks, hoping instead to focus on trade.
